svg.text: MP-SAE (Protocol B) — combined state diagram, A and B
Despite the name “Simultaneous”, Figure 5's wire flow is a strict lockstep: A sends c1, B replies c2, A replies c3, B replies c4.
3 recv C2: compute K_a,v_a, send C3
1 recv C1: make commit, send C2
4 recv C3, v matches: send C4
make_commit(): r,m random mod n=p-1; s=(r+m) mod n; t=g^-m mod p; send; start timer W=2s
resend the identical last frame; after 8 resends -> ERROR (bounded retries, no deadlock)
store (s_b,t_b); K_a=(g^s_b * t_b)^r_a mod p; v_a=prf(KDF(K_a), s_a,t_a,s_b,t_b); send C3
K_b=(g^s_a * t_a)^r_b mod p; v_b=prf(KDF(K_b), s_a,t_a,s_b,t_b); if v_b==v_a(received): send C4, DONE
a repeated c1/c2/c3 (peer's reply was lost) just resends our own last reply; malformed s,t or wrong sender: dropped, never aborts
A checks v_b(received) == its own v_a; match -> A_DONE, mismatch -> A_ERROR (wrong password or forged C4)
K_a == K_b always (not just when r_a+m_a < p): exponents are combined mod the group ORDER n=p-1, not mod the field size p — see sae_mp.c / README.
KDF(K) = Ascon-hash(K)[:16], used as the 16-byte prf() key. v is 16 bytes (the prf() output), reused as both “what I send” and “what I expect from the peer”.
